2607.12200.title: A Threshold Exceedance Framework for CBRN Uplift Evaluation in Frontier Language Models
2607.12200.paper_summary: As frontier language models advance, policymakers and model developers need methods for assessing whether model access materially increases a non-expert actor's ability to plan high-consequence Chemical, Biological, Radiological, or Nuclear (CBRN) misuse relative to public tools alone. Existing CBRN evaluations differ in non-expert definitions, threat scope, baselines, scoring rubrics, and decision rules, making results difficult to compare across studies. We introduce a Threshold Exceedance Criteria (TEC) framework that decomposes an uplift study into independently executable components: determining non-expert participant eligibility, defining the CBRN threat scope for the study, and statistically estimating material uplift. We then operationalize the TEC framework in a large-scale empirical study using a design that determines two forms of uplift: generative (where a model assists plan creation from scratch) and revisionist (where a model assists refinement of an existing plan). The study produced attack plans across the CBRN domains, which we evaluated through subject-matter-expert review to estimate generative and revisionist uplift. Applying the framework, our empirical study revealed domain heterogeneity: under this controlled pre-release evaluation, model-assisted plans sometimes received expert-equivalent instructional ratings, but confirmed material uplift was limited to the radiological domain. These findings informed mitigation and deployment-governance decisions rather than characterizing deployed model behavior. We conclude with methodological lessons for future CBRN uplift evaluations, emphasizing prespecified criteria, explicit baselines, separation of generative and revisionist estimates, and careful distinction between preliminary screening signals and confirmed risk determinations.
2607.12200.paper_summary_zh: 隨著前沿語言模型的進步，政策制定者和模型開發者需要方法來評估模型訪問是否實質性地提高了非專家行為者相對於僅使用公共工具進行高後果化學、生物、放射性或核（CBRN）濫用的能力。現有的CBRN評估在非專家定義、威脅範圍、基準、評分標準和決策規則上存在差異，使得研究結果難以比較。我們引入了一個閾值超越標準（TEC）框架，將提升研究分解為可獨立執行的組件：確定非專家參與者的資格、定義研究的CBRN威脅範圍，以及統計估算實質提升。然後，我們在一項大規模實證研究中將TEC框架進行操作化，該設計確定了兩種形式的提升：生成性（模型從零開始協助計劃創建）和修訂性（模型協助改進現有計劃）。該研究在CBRN領域產生了攻擊計劃，我們通過專家評審進行評估，以估算生成性和修訂性提升。應用該框架，我們的實證研究揭示了領域異質性：在這一受控的預發布評估中，模型輔助的計劃有時獲得了專家等效的指導評級，但確認的實質提升僅限於放射性領域。這些發現為減輕和部署治理決策提供了信息，而不是描述已部署模型的行為。我們總結了未來CBRN提升評估的 методологические уроки，強調預先規定的標準、明確的基準、生成性和修訂性估算的分離，以及初步篩選信號與確認風險判定之間的仔細區分。
